questions.question: Which constitutional amendment gave constitutional status to cooperative societies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**97th Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **97th Constitutional Amendment Act** of **2011** was enacted to provide constitutional status and protection to **cooperative societies** in India, coming into effect on **February 15, 2012**.
 
• It introduced **Article 19(1)(c)** in the **Fundamental Rights** section (Part III), which explicitly grants citizens the right to form **cooperative societies**.
 
• The amendment inserted **Article 43B** into the **Directive Principles of State Policy** (Part IV), directing the State to promote the voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control, and professional management of cooperative societies.
 
• It added a new **Part IXB** to the Constitution, titled **The Co-operative Societies**, spanning **Articles 243ZH to 243ZT**, which regulates the incorporation, number and term of members of the board, and the auditing of accounts.
 
• The primary objective was to ensure that cooperatives across the country operate in a professional and democratic manner, reducing **political interference** and improving economic efficiency for farmers and small-scale producers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **73rd Amendment Act, 1992**:

 
 
• Granted constitutional status to **Panchayati Raj Institutions** by adding **Part IX** and the **Eleventh Schedule** to the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **86th Amendment Act, 2002**:
 
 
• Inserted **Article 21A**, making the **Right to Education** a fundamental right for children between the ages of **6 and 14 years**.
 
 
 
• **91st Amendment Act, 2003**:
 
 
• Limited the size of the **Council of Ministers** to **15 percent** of the total strength of the **Lok Sabha** or **State Legislative Assembly** and strengthened **Anti-Defection** laws.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Cooperation**:
 
 
• In **July 2021**, the Union Government created this ministry to provide a separate administrative, legal, and policy framework for strengthening the cooperative movement under the vision of **Sahkar se Samriddhi**.

questions.question: Which musical instrument is commonly used during Giddha performances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhol**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Giddha** is a popular folk dance of women in the **Punjab** region of India and Pakistan, traditionally performed during social gatherings and festivals like **Teeyan** and **Baisakhi**.
 
• The **Dhol**, a large double-sided barrel drum, is the primary musical instrument that provides the rhythmic foundation for the dance. While **Bhangra** (the male counterpart) uses a larger version, Giddha performances often feature the **Dhol** or its smaller variant, the **Dholki**.
 
• The instrument is typically constructed from a wooden barrel (often **Mango** or **Sheesham** wood) with animal hide stretched over both ends, played using wooden sticks or hands to produce deep bass and sharp treble sounds.
 
• The rhythm of the **Dhol** complements the **Boliyan** (folk singing), where the beat accelerates during the **clapping** sequences, which is a signature element of the Giddha performance.
 
• In a traditional setup, the woman playing the **Dhol** sits in the center of a circle formed by other dancers, who move in rhythmic patterns mimicking daily village chores like churning milk or spinning yarn.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tabla**

 
 
• A set of two small drums used predominantly in **Hindustani classical music** and **Sufi** devotional songs.
 
• It consists of the **Dayan** (treble) and **Bayan** (bass) and is known for its complex finger-tapping techniques rather than the loud, rustic beats required for folk dances.
 
 
 
• **Harmonium**
 
 
• A keyboard-based reed instrument that produces sound by blowing air through bellows; it is a staple in **Ghazals**, **Qawwalis**, and **Kirtans**.
 
• While it provides melodic support in various Punjabi folk genres, it is not the lead rhythmic instrument for Giddha.
 
 
 
• **Sarangi**
 
 
• A short-necked, bowed string instrument made of wood with a skin-covered soundbox, often used to accompany vocalists in **classical** and **folk ballads**.
 
• It is revered for its ability to mimic the nuances of the human voice but is rarely used in the high-energy percussion-centric environment of Giddha.

questions.question: Which physiographic division is famous for its rich alluvial soil and high population density?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Northern Plains**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Northern Plains** of India are formed by the massive depositional work of three major river systems: the **Indus**, the **Ganga**, and the **Brahmaputra**, along with their numerous tributaries.
 
• This physiographic division covers an area of approximately **7 lakh square kilometers**, extending about **2,400 kilometers** in length and **240 to 320 kilometers** in width.
 
• The region is characterized by a deep cover of **alluvial soil**, which has been deposited over millions of years in a vast basin situated at the foothills of the **Himalayas**.
 
• The **alluvium** is extremely fertile and rich in minerals, which, combined with a perennial **water supply** and a **favorable climate**, makes this area the most agriculturally productive part of the country, often referred to as the **granary of India**.
 
• Due to its high **agricultural output** and the flat nature of the terrain, which facilitates easy **transportation** and **urbanization**, the Northern Plains have the **highest population density** among all physiographic divisions in India.
 
• The plains are further categorized into the **Bhabar**, **Terai**, **Bhangar**, and **Khadar** regions based on the variations in relief and the nature of the soil deposits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Peninsular Plateau**:

 
 
• It is a **tableland** composed of old crystalline, **igneous**, and **metamorphic rocks**, formed due to the breaking and drifting of the **Gondwana land**.
 
• This region is known for its **black soil** (Regur) in the **Deccan Trap**, which is ideal for cotton cultivation but is not as densely populated as the Northern Plains.
 
 
 
• **Coastal Plains**:
 
 
• These are narrow coastal strips running along the **Arabian Sea** on the west and the **Bay of Bengal** on the east.
 
• The **Eastern Coastal Plain** features large deltas formed by rivers like the **Mahanadi**, **Godavari**, **Krishna**, and **Kaveri**, which are fertile but much smaller in scale compared to the Northern Plains.
 
 
 
• **Himalayas**:
 
 
• These are **geologically young** and **structurally fold mountains** that stretch across the northern borders of India.
 
• The rugged terrain, steep slopes, and harsh climatic conditions make it unsuitable for intensive agriculture, resulting in a **sparse population density**.

questions.question: Who discovered the electron in 1897 through cathode ray experiments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**J.J. Thomson**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sir Joseph John Thomson**, a British physicist, is credited with the discovery of the **electron** in **1897** through his series of experiments with **cathode ray tubes**.
 
• He observed that **cathode rays** were deflected by both **electric** and **magnetic fields**, suggesting they were composed of **negatively charged particles** rather than waves.
 
• By measuring the degree of deflection, Thomson calculated the **charge-to-mass ratio (e/m)** of these particles and found it to be constant, regardless of the material of the electrodes or the gas in the tube.
 
• He concluded that these particles, which he initially termed **corpuscles**, were a fundamental part of all atoms, thereby proving that the **atom** was divisible.
 
• Following this discovery, he proposed the **Plum Pudding Model** of the atom in **1904**, where negative electrons were embedded in a uniform sphere of positive charge.
 
• Thomson was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics** in **1906** for his work on the conduction of electricity by gases and the discovery of the electron.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ernest Rutherford**:

 
 
• He is known as the **father of nuclear physics**.
 
• Conducted the famous **Gold Foil Experiment** in **1911**, which led to the discovery of the **atomic nucleus**.
 
• He also discovered the **proton** and established that most of the atom's mass is concentrated in the center.
 
 
 
• **Niels Bohr**:
 
 
• Developed the **Bohr Model** of the atom in **1913**.
 
• He proposed that **electrons** revolve around the nucleus in specific **quantized energy levels** or shells.
 
 
 
• **James Chadwick**:
 
 
• He discovered the **neutron** in **1932**.
 
• The neutron is a **subatomic particle** with no net electric charge, located within the **atomic nucleus** along with protons.

questions.question: In KHO-KHO How many defenders enter at the beginning of a defence turn?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the traditional Indian sport of **Kho-Kho**, the game is played between two teams, where one team takes the role of the **chasing side** and the other acts as the **defending side**.
 
• The **defenders** do not enter the field all at once; instead, they follow a systematic **batch system** to ensure the game remains continuous and organized.
 
• At the beginning of a defense turn, exactly **3 defenders** enter the court to face the **chasing team**.
 
• These three players are referred to as a **batch**. Once all three players of the initial batch are declared out, the next batch of **three defenders** must enter the field.
 
• The entry of the next batch must occur before the next **Kho** is signaled by the chaser to a sitting teammate, maintaining the **rhythm of play**.
 
• This rotation continues until the end of the allotted **9-minute turn** for that specific inning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Team Composition and Roles**:

 
 
• A **Kho-Kho team** consists of **12 players** in total, but only **9 players** take the field during a chasing turn (one active chaser and eight sitting chasers).
 
• The **active chaser** can only run in one direction between the **poles** and cannot cross the **central lane** directly.
 
 
 
• **Court Specifications**:
 
 
• The standard dimensions of a **Kho-Kho court** for senior men and women are **27 meters** in length and **16 meters** in width.
 
• The **rectangular field** includes two **wooden poles** fixed at both ends of the **central lane**.
 
 
 
• **Match Format**:
 
 
• A match consists of **two innings**. Each inning contains a chasing and a defending turn for both teams, lasting **9 minutes** each.
 
• The **Kho-Kho Federation of India (KKFI)** is the primary governing body that sets these competitive rules and standards.

questions.question: Which crop is used as both food and fodder in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maize (Zea mays)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Maize (Zea mays)** is recognized as a **dual-purpose crop** in India because it is cultivated both for grain (human food) and for its vegetative parts (animal fodder).
 
• It is popularly known as the **Queen of Cereals** due to its high genetic yield potential and its versatility in adjusting to different **agro-climatic conditions** across the country.
 
• The crop is primarily grown during the **Kharif season**, but in certain states like **Bihar**, it is also a major **Rabi season** crop, highlighting its adaptability.
 
• Geographically, it requires a temperature range of **21°C to 27°C** and performs best in **old alluvial soil** with proper drainage systems.
 
• As a fodder crop, maize is highly valued because it is **highly palatable**, digestible, and can be converted into **silage**, which serves as a nutritious feed for livestock during lean periods.
 
• The use of **High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds** and improved irrigation has made states like **Karnataka**, **Madhya Pradesh**, and **Uttar Pradesh** leading producers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nutritional and Industrial Applications**:

 
 
• Maize contains about **70% starch**, making it a critical industrial raw material for producing **liquid glucose**, **dextrin**, and **corn oil**.
 
• It provides essential nutrients such as **Vitamin A**, **Vitamin E**, and minerals like **iron** and **magnesium** for human diets.
 
 
 
• **Other Crop Contexts**:
 
 
• **Barley (Hordeum vulgare)**: A **Rabi crop** mostly used for human food and as a primary ingredient in the **malting industry** for alcoholic beverages.
 
• **Sugarcane (Saccharum officinarum)**: A major **commercial cash crop** used for manufacturing **sugar**, **gur (jaggery)**, and **khandsari**; its byproduct, bagasse, is used for fuel and paper.
 
• **Jowar (Sorghum bicolor)**: A **coarse grain millet** that is drought-resistant and common in the **Deccan Plateau**, used as both a staple food and forage.

questions.question:
Gurjara-Pratihara Harichandra is known for establishing a kingdom in which region?

I. Tamil Nadu

II. Rajasthan
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Harichandra**, historically known by the title **Rohilladhi**, is recognized as the **progenitor** or founder of the **Gurjara-Pratihara** dynasty during the **6th century AD**.
 
• The early seat of power for this dynasty was established at **Mandavyapura**, which corresponds to the modern-day **Mandore** region in the state of **Rajasthan**. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***
 
• During the period of the early Pratiharas, the region of **Tamil Nadu** was governed by southern dynasties such as the **Pallavas** and the **Pandyas**, and it never fell under the direct administration of the **Gurjara-Pratihara** kingdom. ***Hence, statement I is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dynastic Roots and Expansion**:

 
 
• **Harichandra** was a **Brahmana** king who possessed knowledge of the **Vedas** and **Shastras**; his lineage from a **Kshatriya** wife, **Bhadra**, formed the royal Pratihara line.
 
• His sons—**Bhogabhata**, **Kakka**, **Rajjila**, and **Dadda**—were instrumental in conquering **Mandavyapura** and constructing a defensive **fort** to consolidate their territory.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance**:
 
 
• The **Gurjara-Pratiharas** later became one of the three major powers involved in the **Tripartite Struggle** for the control of **Kannauj** in the **Indo-Gangetic Plain**.
 
• Under rulers like **Nagabhata I**, the dynasty played a crucial role in resisting the **Arab invasions** from **Sindh** during the 8th century, particularly during the **Battle of Rajasthan**.
 
• The **Jodhpur** and **Ghatiyala** inscriptions serve as primary epigraphic sources documenting the origins of **Harichandra** and the early **Pratihara** genealogy.

questions.question: In India, One Nation One Subscription provides access to more than _____ scholarly journals from 30 major international publishers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **One Nation One Subscription (ONOS)** is a landmark initiative by the **Government of India** designed to provide nationwide access to high-quality scholarly literature and research journals.
 
• Under this scheme, the government has negotiated with **30 major international publishers** to provide access to more than **13,000** scholarly journals to all government-funded higher education and research institutions.
 
• The project is spearheaded by the **Ministry of Education** and the **Department of Science and Technology (DST)** to ensure that research resources are not limited by the financial constraints of individual institutions.
 
• The initiative covers approximately **6,300 institutions**, including **Central Universities**, **IITs**, **NITs**, **IISERs**, and various state-funded universities and colleges across India.
 
• The implementation of **ONOS** aims to foster a robust research ecosystem by democratizing access to global knowledge, particularly benefiting students and faculty in smaller or remote educational centers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nodal Agency and Infrastructure:**

 
 
• The **Information and Library Network (INFLIBNET)** Centre, an Inter-University Centre of the **University Grants Commission (UGC)**, acts as the nodal agency for the execution and management of the **ONOS** portal.
 
• The initiative aligns with the goals of the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**, which emphasizes research, innovation, and the use of technology in education.
 
• By consolidating subscriptions at a national level, the government achieves significant **cost-efficiency** and eliminates the duplication of efforts and payments by individual institutions.
 
• It supports the **Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF)** vision to elevate India's global standing in scientific and academic research.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of question asked in the Indian parliament?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Urgent Question**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Starred Questions** are those for which a member desires an **oral answer** on the floor of the House. These are distinguished by an **asterisk mark**. Because the answer is delivered orally, **supplementary questions** can be asked by members with the permission of the Speaker or Chairman. Hence, Starred Question is a valid type.
 
• **Unstarred Questions** are those for which a **written explanation** is required. These are not specifically marked with an asterisk, and the written reply is deemed to be laid on the table of the House by the concerned Minister at the end of **Question Hour**. No **supplementary questions** can follow these. Hence, Unstarred Question is a valid type.
 
• **Short Notice Questions** relate to matters of **urgent public importance** and can be asked with a notice shorter than the standard **ten clear days**. These questions are answered **orally**, provided the Minister concerned agrees to answer at short notice. Hence, Short Notice is a valid type.
 
• The Indian parliamentary system does not recognize a category formally named **Urgent Question**. While the **Short Notice Question** addresses urgent matters, the terminology 'Urgent Question' is not used in the **Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business** of the **Lok Sabha** or **Rajya Sabha**. Hence, Urgent Question is not a type of parliamentary question.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Question Hour**:

 
 
• It is the **first hour** of every parliamentary sitting where members of Parliament (MPs) exercise their right to hold the **Executive** accountable.
 
• Questions can also be addressed to **Private Members** if the subject matter relates to a **Bill** or **Resolution** for which that member is responsible.
 
 
 
• **Zero Hour**:
 
 
• This is an **Indian parliamentary innovation** that is not mentioned in the **Rules of Procedure**.
 
• It starts immediately after the Question Hour and lasts until the **regular agenda** of the House is taken up.

questions.question: India added ____ new species to its fauna in the year 2024.
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

The monitoring and documentation of animal diversity in India are carried out by the **Zoological Survey of India (ZSI)**, a premier organization under the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change**. Every year, the ZSI releases a publication titled **'Animal Discoveries'**, which catalogs new species discovered (new to science) and new records (species found in India for the first time) during the preceding calendar year.

The relation used to determine the total additions is:

Total Faunal Additions = **New Species discovered** + **New Records** for the country

Given

The report released in the year **2024** (detailing discoveries from the year **2023**) by the **Zoological Survey of India (ZSI)**.

Calculation

In **July 2024**, during the **109th Foundation Day** of the **Zoological Survey of India**, the Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, **Bhupender Yadav**, released the **'Animal Discoveries 2023'** report. According to the data compiled in this comprehensive survey:

1. Scientists and researchers identified a significant number of species across different geographical zones including the **Western Ghats**, **North-East India**, and the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**.

2. The total number of faunal taxa added to the Indian database as per the specific data release for that period was **683**.

3. This total includes **invertebrates** (which comprise the majority, particularly **insects**) and **vertebrates** (such as **reptiles**, **fishes**, and **mammals**).

4. With these additions, the total faunal diversity of India has reached a new milestone, reinforcing India's status as a **mega-biodiverse** nation.

Final Answer: ✅ 683

questions.question: The Combat Air Teaming System (CATS) Warrior, an advanced unmanned aerial vehicle concept, has been developed by which organization in May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**HAL**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Combat Air Teaming System (CATS) Warrior** is an indigenous **unmanned combat aerial vehicle (UCAV)** concept spearheaded by **Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL)**.
 
• It is designed as a **loyal wingman**, an autonomous platform intended to fly in tandem with manned fighter aircraft such as the **LCA Tejas** or the upcoming **AMCA**.
 
• The system utilizes **Manned-Unmanned Teaming (MUM-T)** technology, which allows human pilots to command a fleet of drones to perform **Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR)** or **strike missions**.
 
• The **Warrior** is designed to carry a variety of munitions, including air-to-air and air-to-ground missiles, and is powered by a twin-engine configuration utilizing modified **PTAE-7** turbojet engines.
 
• By deploying the **Warrior** for high-risk operations, the **Indian Air Force (IAF)** can effectively penetrate contested airspaces while significantly reducing the risk to human pilots and expensive manned assets.
 
• The project is a critical component of India’s **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative, aiming for self-reliance in advanced **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** based combat technologies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL)**:

 
 
• Established in **1940** and headquartered in **Bengaluru**, it is a premier **Navratna** Central Public Sector Enterprise under the **Ministry of Defence**.
 
• HAL is responsible for the design and manufacture of the **LCA Tejas**, **LCH Prachand**, and **HTT-40** trainer aircraft.
 
 
 
• **CATS Ecosystem Components**:
 
 
• **CATS Hunter**: A standoff, air-launched cruise missile designed to hit targets deep within enemy territory.
 
• **CATS ALFA (Air-Launched Flexible Asset)**: A specialized carrier capable of releasing **swarm drones** to overwhelm and saturate enemy air defenses.
 
• **CATS Infinity**: A **High-Altitude Pseudo-Satellite (HAPS)** designed for ultra-long endurance flights for persistent surveillance and communication relay.
 
 
 
• **DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation)**:
 
 
• While **DRDO** focuses on broader military R&D, including the **Tapal-BH** and **Ghatak** UCAV projects, the **CATS Warrior** is specifically an **HAL-led** innovation.

questions.question: Which Indian city hosted the World Para Athletics Championships in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**New Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Para Athletics Championships**:

• **Paralympic Committee of India (PCI)**:

• It is recognized by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**, Government of India, and is actively involved in training and selecting athletes for international meets.
 
 
 
• **New Delhi's Sporting Legacy**:

• Key venues like the **Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium** offer world-class, barrier-free infrastructure tailored to meet the accessibility needs of para-athletes.

questions.question: In India, the design of Swachh Survekshan survey is based on how many key pillars?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Swachh Survekshan** is an annual survey of cleanliness, hygiene, and sanitation in cities and towns across India, launched as part of the **Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban)**.
 
• The design and assessment methodology of the survey are fundamentally built upon **three key pillars** that determine the final rankings of the **Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)**.
 
• The first pillar is **Service Level Progress (SLP)**, which accounts for a significant portion of the total score. It evaluates the performance of cities in **segregated waste collection**, processing, disposal, and **sustainable sanitation** through data submitted by the local authorities.
 
• The second pillar is **Certification**, which involves third-party verification of cities. This includes ratings under the **Star Rating Protocol for Garbage-Free Cities (GFC)** and various **Open Defecation Free (ODF, ODF+, ODF++)** certifications.
 
• The third pillar is **Citizens Voice**, which emphasizes direct feedback from residents. It measures **citizen engagement**, awareness, and satisfaction through surveys, the **Swachhata App**, and innovative initiatives led by the community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)**:

 
 
• This is the nodal ministry responsible for conducting the **Swachh Survekshan** survey annually since its inception in **2016**.
 
• The first survey in **2016** covered only **73 cities**, but it has grown to become the **world largest urban sanitation survey**, covering over **4,000 cities**.
 
 
 
• **Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM)**:
 
 
• Launched on **October 2, 2014**, to commemorate the **145th birth anniversary** of **Mahatma Gandhi**.
 
• The mission aims to achieve **100% scientific management** of municipal solid waste and eliminate **open defecation** across India.
 
• The **2023** edition of the survey was themed **Waste to Wealth**, highlighting the importance of **circular economy** principles in waste management.

questions.question: Which country was the world's largest importer of arms in 2020-24 as per SIPRI report published in March 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ukraine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI)** report released in **March 2025**, **Ukraine** has emerged as the world's largest arms importer for the period **2020-24**.
 
• The surge in imports is a direct result of the large-scale military aid and procurement following the **Russian invasion** in **2022**, which fundamentally altered the global arms trade landscape.
 
• Prior to **2022**, Ukraine was not a major importer, but it surpassed long-standing top importers like **India** and **Saudi Arabia** due to the influx of **heavy artillery**, **air defense systems**, and **armored vehicles** from the **United States** and **NATO** allies.
 
• The **SIPRI** data utilizes **Trend Indicator Values (TIV)** to measure the volume of transfers of major conventional weapons rather than the financial value of the contracts.
 
• The report also highlighted that **Europe** nearly doubled its arms imports between **2015-19** and **2020-24**, reflecting heightened security concerns across the continent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **SIPRI (Stockholm International Peace Research Institute)**:

 
 
• Founded in **1966**, it is an independent international institute that researches **conflict**, **armaments**, **arms control**, and **disarmament**.
 
• It provides open-source data on **military expenditure** and **international arms transfers**, serving as a primary resource for global security analysis.
 
 
 
• **Japan**:
 
 
• Japan has significantly increased its arms imports in the **2020-24** period to enhance its **long-range strike capabilities** and **maritime defense** in response to regional tensions in the **Indo-Pacific**.
 
 
 
• **Brazil**:
 
 
• Brazil is a major defense actor in **Latin America**, focusing on strategic projects like the **Prosub** submarine program and the acquisition of **Gripen** fighter jets to modernize its **air force** and **navy**.
 
 
 
• **North Korea**:
 
 
• Subject to strict **United Nations Security Council** sanctions, North Korea is prohibited from legal arms imports and exports, focusing instead on **indigenous development** of **ballistic missiles** and **nuclear technology**.
